title: Greater Manchester Police arrest alleged driver in 100mph stolen Amazon van pursuit

input.lead: A suspected thief is held after leading police on a 40-minute chase in a stolen Amazon van
input.summary: A suspected thief is held after leading police on a 40-minute chase in a stolen Amazon van
input.evidence_text: A suspected thief was arrested after leading traffic police on a 100mph chase in a stolen Amazon delivery van carrying £1,000 worth of parcels The 25-year-old was held after officers pursued the van from Wigan, in Greater Manchester, through Bolton and into Chorley in Lancashire, where the van crashed into pedestrian barriers and a vehicle stopped at traffic lights Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said over the course of 40 minutes, the van had been driven three times over the speed limit, reaching around 100mph, injured a cyclist and caused significant damage to multiple pieces of street furniture No serious injuries were reported. The arrested man has been bailed pending further inquiries GMP received a 999 call at around 18:23 BST on Wednesday to report the van had been stolen Officers located the vehicle within 15 minutes and began to follow it. They tried to stop it without a pursuit, but the driver sped away

title: Mayor wants to see Stockport regeneration inspire other areas

input.lead: Mayor of Greater Manchester Bev Craig wants other areas to follow Stockport's lead
input.summary: Mayor of Greater Manchester Bev Craig wants other areas to follow Stockport's lead
input.evidence_text: The mayor of Greater Manchester has said she hopes the £1bn regeneration of Stockport town centre can be replicated in towns across the region The Stockport Mayoral Development Corporation (MDC) was launched seven years ago and has ambitions to build 8,000 new homes in the town centre by 2040 Bev Craig, who became metro mayor of Greater Manchester in July, said: "I want to carry on and go further with the work of Mayoral Development Corporations across the region "I want to build genuinely affordable homes on publicly owned land and, by getting the private sector to back us, I'm excited about what we can achieve with our MDCs, in places like Ashton-under-Lyne, Stalybridge and Oldham." input.evidence_text: Real Life 'I got the s**t kicked out of me - but it made me realise who I needed to help' Advisor to some of the UK and US' top politicians, 32-yera-old Pablo O'Hana from Withington left school with few qualifications and never went to university View Comments News Lee Grimsditch Features Writer 06:34, 16 Aug 2026 Walking into Westminster's Strangers' Bar on his third day in Parliament, brand-new political staffer Pablo O'Hana came up against the stuffy elitism of British politics. Aged 19 and a brand-new staffer for Mancheste The question took Pablo aback; not only did it come barely seconds after their introduction, but its meaning wasn't immediately obvious. He soon realised the MP was referring to which university he attended: "Oxford or Cambridge?" The surreal moment made him realise just how at odds his own upbringing in Withington was compared to the MPs and staffers he would now rub shoulders with at the bar. input.summary: Wigan Council is reminding residents to recycle electrical items responsibly this summer due to dangers posed to waste collection crews As temperatures rise and the use of electrical items such as fans, portable chargers, and other rechargeable items increase, the council is urgi
input.evidence_text: Wigan Council is reminding residents to recycle electrical items responsibly this summer due to dangers posed to waste collection crews As temperatures rise and the use of electrical items such as fans, portable chargers, and other rechargeable items increase, the council is urging residents to ensure unwanted electricals are taken to the correct recycling facilities Research from Material Focus has highlighted the growing popularity of low-cost electrical products, often known as ‘FastTech’, which can be easily forgotten, thrown away, or incorrectly disposed of. Many of these items contain batteries and valuable materials that can be recover When electrical items are placed in black and brown bins, they can also become damaged during collection and processing. This can cause batteries to spark, leading to fires that put waste and recycling crews at risk and can cause significant damage to vehicles and facilities Councillor Paul Kenny, portfolio holder for planning, environmental services and transport, said: "We know that during periods of hot weather, fans are often essential items to help people cool down, but when these products reach the end of their life, they should never be thrown "Electrical items and batteries can cause fires if damaged, putting our collection crews and staff at risk. By taking unwanted electricals to the correct recycling point, residents can help protect our workers, reduce waste, and ensure valuable materials are recovered and reused

Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

title: Maresca fitness update on McAidoo, Haaland and Rodri

input.lead: Maresca fitness update on McAidoo, Haaland and Rodri
input.summary: But the new City boss says that he needs to consider that many of his squad have only just returned after being given time off after playing in the World Cup. The Italian will have the opportunity to fight for his first trophy since taking charge when we face the Gunners at the P
input.evidence_text: But the new City boss says that he needs to consider that many of his squad have only just returned after being given time off after playing in the World Cup. The Italian will have the opportunity to fight for his first trophy since taking charge when we face the Gunners at the Principality Stadium for the 15:00 (UK) kick-off. Players that reached the quarter-finals or beyond missed our pre-season tour to Asia, which could potentially impact team selection for the game. Of those that did travel to Hong Kong and South Korea, winger Ryan McAidoo is the only player to suffer a setback, picking up a slight shoulder issue from the first game against Inter. “The only one is Ryan McAidoo who in pre-season had a small problem but he has already worked with us,” Maresca said at his pre-match news conference. “So everyone is fit knowing that some of them just arrived two days ago.” Fans got an opportunity to see the players at our City Are Back open training session at the Joie Stadium earlier this week. Erling Haaland sat out some of the training but Maresca says he is fine for the start of the season. “Yes he was okay,” he added. “He just had some small things behind his heels but he’s okay.” Maresca confirmed that Rodri is back at the CFA after successful minor back surgery following the World Cup. “He’s now in rehab,” the boss added. “When he’s ready to start training session with us, this is the problem for him.” Premier League 2026/27 home tickets now on sale General admission tickets for Manchester City’s home 2026/27 Premier League fixtures are now on sale to Premium, Matchday and Junior Members.
